objective: Settle the two facts the remaining T3 work needs: how holyagent setup can set per-project T3 git settings, and whether the pinned rpiv ask-user and todo Pi packages render through custom() TUI components.
scope: Earlier T3 research: /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw8tdgpq-hfsl.md (read first). T3 Code source: github.com/pingdotgg/t3code (main, and the v0.1.7 tag where readable; raw.githubusercontent.com works where the GitHub API does not).

A. result:
result: Both questions are answered from source, but the T3 and rpiv files were read from `main`, not the pinned tags. Setup can't safely key a project before T3 has opened it, and `t3.json` cannot carry the git keys. Both rpiv packages degrade without `custom()` as shown in the rpiv section below.

**A. T3 per-project settings** (sources: `raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/main/packages/contracts/src/{settings,pullRequest}.ts` and `docs/user/project-settings.md`, plus the git.cafe and VibedByKaKi mirrors)
**ProjectId (sourced):** it is a random UUID v4, not a path hash or git-remote hash.
  - `apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts` has `newProjectId = () => ProjectId.make(randomUUID())`.
  - The `t3 project add` CLI (`apps/server/src/cli/project.ts`) does `ProjectId.make(yield* projectCommandUuid)`, which is `crypto.randomUUIDv4`, then dispatches `project.create` with `workspaceRoot`.
  - The id is stored in T3's event-sourced orchestration database. The server rejects a second active project with the same normalized `workspaceRoot`.
  - **Keying before T3 opens a project (inference):** an external tool cannot derive the id from the repository. It could only pick a UUID and run `t3 project add <path>`, but the UUID is minted inside that command and printed ("Added project <id> ..."). Setup would have to run that command and parse the id, or read the id from the read model after the project is added. The `project.create` command accepts any client-supplied `projectId`, but I did not find a CLI flag that lets you set it.
**`t3.json` (sourced):** it sits at the repository root, with schema `https://t3.codes/schema/t3.json` (PR #4317). The schema file is `t3ProjectFile.ts`, read only on the mirror.
  - Keys: `$schema`, `iconPath`, `defaultThreadEnvMode` (`local` or `worktree`), `worktreeSubmodules` (`recursive`, `top-level` or `none`), and `scripts` (at most 50).
  - `PROJECT_FILE_BACKED_SETTINGS` lists only `defaultThreadEnvMode` and `worktreeSubmodules`.
  - So `branchNamingMode`, `branchNamePrefix`, `branchNameInstructions` and `pullRequestMergeMethod` are not in the mirror's `t3.json` schema.
  - The main docs say "settings a repository can also declare in t3.json, such as...". That is open-ended, so a newer `main` could have added keys.
  - The mirror may be older than `main`, so I could not verify the live schema.
**`projectSettingsOverrides` (sourced):**
  - It is a record in the server `settings.json`, keyed by ProjectId.
  - Each entry is `ProjectSettingsOverrides`; an absent key inherits.
  - `branchNamingMode` is `static`, `semantic` or `custom`. `branchNamePrefix` and `branchNameInstructions` are trimmed strings. `pullRequestMergeMethod` is nullable.
  - The PR #11176 text says patches replace a project's entry wholesale and `null` removes it.
  - `pullRequestMergeMethod: null` "keeps using the method last chosen on the device".
**Environment-wide fallback (sourced):** the same four keys also exist at server level with defaults `static`, `"t3"`, `""` and `null`. These need no ProjectId.
**`PullRequestMergeMethod` (sourced):** `"merge" | "squash" | "rebase"`.
**`pullRequestMergeMethodOverrides` (sourced for shape, inferred for key meaning):**
  - It is in `ClientSettingsSchema`, so it is device-local, not in server `settings.json`.
  - Its type is `Record<TrimmedNonEmptyString, PullRequestMergeMethod>`.
  - The PR #11176 text calls it the legacy client-only per-project map, folded into the record. The key is therefore a per-project string, presumably the project id or repository identity. I did not find the exact key source.

**B. rpiv packages**
Sources are `raw.githubusercontent.com/juicesharp/rpiv-mono/main/packages/.../*.ts`. The unpkg 2.15.0 file listings confirm the same files exist (`rpc-fallback.ts`, `ask-user-question.ts`, `todo-overlay.ts`), but unpkg `.ts` fetches failed. File contents may differ slightly from the 2.15.0 tarball.

**`ask-user-question`: tool and parameters.** The tool name is `ask_user_question`, from `ask-user-question.ts` `ASK_USER_QUESTION_TOOL_NAME`. Parameters are in `tool/types.ts`.
  - Shape: `{questions[1..4]: {question, header(<=16 chars), options[2..4]: {label(<=60), description, preview?}, multiSelect?}}`.
**`ask-user-question`: `ctx.ui` calls.**
  - TUI path: `ctx.ui.custom` (`mountQuestionnaire`), plus `notify` and `onTerminalInput`.
  - RPC path (`rpc-fallback.ts`): `ui.select(title, options)` and `ui.input(title, placeholder)` only.
  - It makes no `confirm`, `editor`, `setWidget` or `setStatus` calls.
**`ask-user-question`: RPC behaviour.**
  - `execute` returns a `no_ui` error if `!ctx.hasUI`.
  - If `ctx.mode === "rpc"` and the host has `select` and `input`, it goes straight to the dialog walker and never calls `custom()`.
  - If `custom()` resolves `undefined`, `resolveUndefinedResult` runs the same walker when `select` and `input` exist. Otherwise it returns a `no_custom_ui` error telling the model to ask in plain text.
  - Under T3 this means each question is a `select` dialog. "Type something." and multi-select use `input`. Preview text is folded into the title.
  - The walker also handles hosts that return free text from `select`; the source names T3 Code's "Type your own answer" box (#299).
  - A dismissed dialog cancels the whole questionnaire.
**`todo`: tool and parameters.** The tool name is `todo` and the slash command is `/todos`.
  - The action enum is `create|update|list|get|delete|clear`.
  - The parameter names I saw are `id`, `status`, `activeForm`, `blockedBy`, `addBlockedBy`, `removeBlockedBy` and `includeDeleted`. The `subject` and `description` fields are inferred from the prompt text.
  - I did not read the exact `TodoParamsSchema` in `tool/types.ts`.
**`todo`: `ctx.ui` calls.** The tool `execute` makes no `ctx.ui` calls and works in any mode.
  - The widget (`todo-overlay.ts`) calls `setWidget("rpiv-todos", factory, {placement:"aboveEditor"})`. The factory is `(tui, theme) => ({render, invalidate})`, which is a custom-component widget, not a string array.
  - Clearing it calls `setWidget(key, undefined)`.
  - It also uses `getToolsExpanded?.()`, and the `/todos` command uses `notify`.
  - It calls no `custom`, `select`, `input`, `confirm`, `editor` or `setStatus`.
**`todo`: RPC behaviour.**
  - There is no `ctx.mode` check. The overlay is set up only when `ctx.hasUI`.
  - Per the earlier T3 report, T3 ignores `setWidget`. The overlay is therefore invisible, but the tool still works and returns text results.
  - Whether Pi's RPC mode invokes the factory form is not sourced.

evidence:
Question A is answered with sources, including whether setup can key a project before T3 opens it and whether t3.json can carry the git keys: ProjectId is a random UUID v4 (`apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts`, `apps/server/src/cli/project.ts`) and no external derivation exists. `t3.json` has no git keys (mirror `t3ProjectFile.ts`, `PROJECT_FILE_BACKED_SETTINGS`). The merge enum is `merge|squash|rebase`. The `pullRequestMergeMethodOverrides` key meaning is only inferred.
Question B is answered per package with the ctx.ui calls and rpc behaviour, with source lines: `ask-user-question.ts` (`viaRpc`, `runTuiPath`, `resolveUndefinedResult`), `rpc-fallback.ts` (`DialogUI`, `runRpcQuestionnaire`), `todo-overlay.ts` (`setWidget`), and `todo.ts` / `index.ts` (no `ctx.ui` calls in `execute`, no `mode` check).
answers: sections A and B above.
